reconstructed_theorem_text: Let E be any finite-dimensional real inner-product space with its induced norm and Borel sigma-algebra. Let gamma_E be the centered Gaussian probability measure on E with covariance the identity. Let L^2(gamma_E; R) be the real Hilbert space of square-integrable real-valued functions modulo gamma_E-almost-everywhere equality. For every real polynomial p, there exists a family h of square-integrability witnesses, one for every w in E, such that f_w(x)=p(<w,x>) is gamma_E-almost-everywhere strongly measurable and has finite squared integral, and the map F_p:E -> L^2(gamma_E; R), F_p(w)=[f_w], formed using h(w), is infinitely continuously Frechet differentiable over R on all of E. The family h is quantified after E and p and covers every w; smoothness is in the L^2 norm with respect to w.
objects: The literal functions f_w(x)=p(<w,x>) and their L^2 classes F_p(w).
domains: E as above; p in R[t]; w and x in E; F_p has codomain L^2(gamma_E; R).
quantifiers: For every E and p, there exists h with h(w):MemLp(f_w,2,gamma_E) for every w, and the class-valued map formed with h is C^infinity.
assumptions: Finite-dimensional real inner-product structure, compatible norm, and Borel measurable structure only; p is arbitrary.
conclusion: All f_w belong to MemLp at exponent 2, and w |-> [f_w] is C^infinity over R.
scopes: Global ambient-domain Frechet smoothness for all w in E, valued in the genuine L^2 quotient.
constant_dependencies: The family h and map F_p may depend on E and p. The Gaussian is fixed by E and its inner product. No numerical bound or auxiliary constant is quantified.
semantic_notes: The existential witness h is an all-w integrability proof family, not an arbitrary choice of feature map.
The smoothness order is infinity, not analyticity. There is no unit-norm restriction on w.
